nodes.nodeTitle:
Oftentimes other systems need to use the inputs used by Mover, such as camera or animation. In order to keep these systems in sync with Mover, its good practice to retrieve the inputs FROM Mover, rather than using the same inputs sent TO Mover. This is because Mover can update at a different tick rate than the pawn, and also due to the fact that Mover will automatically replicate the inputs its given. This simply caches those inputs for ease of use across this BP, so that we dont have to do a long string of functions each time we need the data.

For clarity, there are two sets of input structs. "_PreSim" are the values sent TO Mover in the Produce Input interface function. These values are non replicated and will only be set on locally controlled pawns. "_PostSim" are the values retrieved FROM mover, and are safe to use to control other systems.

nodes.nodeTitle: Now that we have the Movement Direction Angle and the desired Movement Direction, we can determine how to offset the pawn's rotation. We do this via curve assets for easy control, since each direction may need slightly different offset behavior. These curve assets are stored in a chooser and are selected based on the MovementDirection and MovementMode, and the Movement Direction Angle is used as the InTime for the curves. The curve value (y axis) at the InTime (x axis) determines the Rotation Offset angle passed into mover.

nodes.nodeTitle: When the Strafe or Aim style is 1, the character will only use the forward and backward directions. This is a relatively experimental style of locomotion but creates a very natural look and feel, well suited for non-combat exploration in games that still need the pawn to rotate to face the aiming direction. This function returns the RotationMode, which represents the overall rotation behavior of the pawn. This will vary from game to game and is typically determined by the game genre (top down, action adventure, shooter, etc), or by other gameplay states.

For demo purposes, we've provided 3 main rotation types.

Orient To Movement - The pawn will rotate to face the direction of movement (standard 3rd person action/adventure).

Strafe - The pawn will loosely rotate to face the aiming rotation while moving (TLoU, GOW, Allan Wake, etc)

Aim - The pawn will always rotate to face the pawn rotation with minimal offset (standard behavior when aiming a weapon or in many over the shoulder 3rd person games).

nodes.nodeTitle:
This function is responsible for gathering "inputs" for Mover, and is called by Mover (only on locally controlled pawns) before it simulates. "Inputs" are simply bits of data that Mover can use during its simulation update. The movement modes themselves have the final authority for how to interpret these inputs, therefore these inputs can be treated like requests or suggestions. For example, "Jump Just Pressed" may only be respected when the pawn is in a Walking movement mode.

These bits of data are stored in structs (some are already provided but they can also be User Defined Structs), and then added to an "Input Collection", which is essentially a container of input structs, which is then added to an Input Cmd Context (which for now only contains an Input Collection) and passed to Mover.

Although this function is only called on locally controlled pawns, the inputs are sent to the server and optionally replicated to simulated proxies (if Sync Inputs for Sim Proxy is true). This means as long as things like anim graphs are controlled by inputs retrieved from the mover component, they should replicate fine without additional work.

Since Mover is still experimental, some of this (like which input structs are pre provided by mover) is liable to change.

A specific input struct can be pulled from the collection using the "Get Data From Collection" function. Since this function's output starts as a wildcard, you must feed in the specific struct you are trying to retrieve.
